claim: O'aka can pay its cost with a Saga's lore counter. Remove the only lore counter from Summon: Valefor after chapter I has resolved, and the Saga goes back to 1 at your next precombat main phase, so chapter I bounces each opponent's most expensive creature again. That costs a commander tempo twice for one card and draws you a card as well.
evidence: Game 0031, turn 17: Valefor's chapter I sent all three commanders back to hand, and O'aka then drew Swords to Plowshares by removing the lore counter. On turn 21 chapter I fired again and bounced Mothman, Edgar and Party Thrasher. That cleared the skies for the 14-damage Valefor swing that knocked out Mothman.

claim: Before combat, pile every counter source onto one evasive or trampling creature: The Ozolith, Fight Rigging, Innkeeper's Talent, Blitzball Stadium's support, Elspeth's +1, and Tidus's own counter move. Let Sagas and creatures that are about to die put their counters on The Ozolith. Then swing for the kill or for 21 commander damage.
evidence: Game 0031, turn 21: Valefor collected counters from Ozolith, Fight Rigging, Innkeeper's Talent, Stadium and Tidus and hit Mothman for 14, exactly lethal. On turn 27 Valefor was sacrificed at chapter IV and its 11 counters went onto The Ozolith, then onto Tidus. Tidus trampled 16 through two blockers onto Edgar, then hit Zuko for 25 commander damage on turn 29.

Game 0041. On turn 14 Tidus hit Fire Lord Zuko for 5. On turn 18 he had 8 counters and was unblockable, and he hit Zuko for 11, reaching 16 commander damage in two swings. The auditor flagged that the Stadium had not been tapped to pay for Go for the Goal.

Game 0052: Forge of Heroes gave Tidus a counter on the turn he entered (round 4). Elspeth then made him a 5/5 flier (round 5), and each Cheer grew him further. He hit Miirym for 5, 6, 7 and 9, killing her with 27 commander damage in round 8. The pilot passed on moving counters off him on turn 28 to keep the damage on one body.

claim: Use Tidus's beginning-of-combat move for more than +1/+1 counters: it can take a stun counter off a creature you need and put it on one that is not attacking. And when you choose a Saga for proliferate (Cheer), it must also get a lore counter, so leave the Saga out of the proliferate if you don't want its chapters to move on.
evidence: Game 0031, turn 24: Zuko redirected Valefor's chapter II so it stunned Valefor itself, and Tidus's combat trigger moved that stun counter onto the freshly cast Kutzil. On the same turn the pilot proliferated Valefor's +1/+1 counters but skipped its lore counter. The auditor ruled it had to add the lore counter too.

Game 0062 turn 25: the pilot tried to proliferate Yojimbo's +1/+1 counter while skipping its lore counter; the auditor ruled the lore counter must come too, chapter IV made 2 Treasures (which paid for Kami of Whispered Hopes on turn 28), and Yojimbo died with 6 counters, so Yuna put 6 +1/+1 counters on Tidus, taking him from 2 counters to 8 (11/11).

claim: Keep one white open for Swords to Plowshares or Path to Exile on opponents' turns, and use it on an attacking commander once a pump like double strike is announced, rather than on your own turn. Answering in response makes their trick fizzle and sends the commander back to the command zone.
evidence: Game 0031, turn 26: Edgar Markov cast Boros Charm for double strike while attacking. With Boros Charm still on the stack, the pilot exiled Edgar with Swords from its held Plains. That stopped 12 commander damage, and the Charm lost its target.

Game 0041. Path was in hand from round 2 and The Wise Mothman (a flier) landed on turn 16. On turn 18 Tidus tapped all five lands, including both white sources, and on turn 20 the Mothman hit for 9 commander damage while Path could not be cast. On turn 24 Path was cast into the Mothman's open Forest and Temple and met Heroic Intervention. The 17 damage that followed made 26 commander damage and knocked Tidus out.

Game 0052, round 6 (turn 25): the pilot left a Plains open with Swords. Zuko flashed Embercleave onto an attacking Bonehoard Dracosaur (8/8 double strike, trample, 16 damage). Swords exiled it in response, and Embercleave fell off. (Put right by the fact check: Turn 25 was Fire Lord Zuko's turn at the start of round 7. The Plains were left untapped on Tidus's round-6 turn (turn 24), and after Herald was cast both Plains were open. Swords exiling the Embercleave-equipped Bonehoard Dracosaur during Zuko's attack is correct.)

claim: Before keeping, count the lands that make each of G, W and U on their own. Flooded Grove, Forge of Heroes, Nesting Grounds, Overflowing Basin, Skycloud Expanse and Sungrass Prairie make no colour alone. A seven whose only coloured sources are one colour, with blue creatures and nothing under 3 mana, does nothing before turn 3–4, so mulligan it when the mulligan is free.
evidence: Game 0052, setup and rounds 1–2: the kept hand was Plains, Plains, Flooded Grove, Forge of Heroes, Rikku, Herald and Damning Verdict. It had no blue source, so Rikku and Herald were uncastable. The seat cast nothing in rounds 1–2, and the first spell (Kami, round 3) came from a drawn Temple of Mystery.

claim: Once every creature you control has a counter, Damning Verdict is a one-sided wipe. Cast it when an opponent has lethal-size counterless attackers pointed at you, even if that means skipping a held trick. Your life total also has to survive the players you aren't racing.
evidence: Game 0052, round 7 (turn 28): the pilot was at 27 life with 6 lands open. Miirym had Miirym, two Goldspan Dragons and two Wrathful Red Dragons, all without counters, while Tidus, Herald and every other creature on the table had counters. The pilot wrote that it would cast Verdict, then cast Lulu and held Ripples instead. Miirym's dragons then hit for 24 and left it at 3. At 2 life after its rad mill, it died to Fire Lord Zuko's Chandra's Ignition through Heartfire Hero on turn 32.

claim: Before casting Farewell (or any mass exile) check that The Ozolith or Resourceful Defense is on the battlefield to catch your counters; if neither is, Farewell erases your own investment and your commander returns at +2 tax with nothing on him. Game 0062 turn 28: Tidus was an 11/11 with 8 +1/+1 counters and had just put 11 commander damage on Miirym (33 to 22, 10 more to win), and Farewell exiled him and Yuna along with the Dragons — Tidus came back on turn 30 for 7 mana as a bare 3/3 and never got above 9/9 again.
evidence: Game 0062, round 8 (table turn 28): after hitting Miirym for 11 with an 11/11 Tidus, the pilot cast Farewell in main 2 choosing creatures and enchantments, exiling its own Tidus and Yuna; Miirym replayed Lathliss on turn 29 and had Ganax, Ureni and Ancient Silver Dragon by turn 31, attacking this seat for 7 and then 21.

claim: Do not attack with a counter-loaded Tidus into a defender holding three or more untapped creatures unless you have granted evasion first (Herald of Secret Streams, Rikku, Blitzball Stadium's Go for the Goal, or trample from Duskshell Crawler or Sphere Grid). Gang blocks kill him and every +1/+1 counter on him is gone, since Luminous Broodmoth returns him as a bare 3/3 with a flying counter, not with his counters.
evidence: Game 0062 round 10 (turn 32): the note reasoned 'Unblocked: she reaches 20 commander damage' while Miirym had six untapped creatures; three 5/5 Dragon tokens blocked, Tidus killed one and died, and Broodmoth returned him with a flying counter and none of his six +1/+1 counters.

claim: Summon: Yojimbo's chapter I exiles a *tapped* creature, so aim it at an opposing commander that has already attacked — it goes to the command zone and costs tax to return. Then its chapters II and III tax every attacker {2}, which is why you can afford to cast it with your board empty.
evidence: Game 0062 round 5 (turn 17): Yojimbo's chapter I exiled Fire Lord Zuko, tapped from his turn-14 attack, sending him to the command zone; chapters II and III on turns 21 and 25 taxed attacks, and this seat lost 0 life to combat from turn 17 through turn 28 while it built up.

claim: When you are down to one opponent whose threats all fly and you control nothing that blocks them, spend the turn on the flying bodies you already have — on turn 30 that was Luminous Broodmoth, held since round 6, plus the Grateful Apparition that Yuna's Whistle found that same turn (Thrummingbird was not drawn until turn 32) — before paying a high commander tax; a freshly recast Tidus is summoning sick, blocks no flier, and a turn later he still cannot attack profitably. With ~12 mana on turn 30 the pilot instead spent 3 on Yuna's Whistle and 7 recasting Tidus, wasting a floating W; Lathliss hit for 7 on turn 31 and the flying blockers only arrived on turn 32.
evidence: Game 0062 round 9 (turn 30): with ~12 mana (6 lands plus Kami tapping for 6) the pilot spent 3 on Yuna's Whistle and 7 recasting Tidus, wasting a floating W, while writing 'Her Lathliss is a 7/7 flier, and I have nothing that can block fliers'; Luminous Broodmoth had been in hand since round 6. Lathliss hit for 7 on turn 31, and Broodmoth, Together Forever, Grateful Apparition and Thrummingbird all came down together on turn 32, one turn too late. (Put right by the fact check: WHAT HAPPENED TO EACH CARD shows Thrummingbird first seen in round 10 (turn 32) and played the same round, so it was not in hand on turn 30 and could not have been cast a turn earlier. Grateful Apparition was first seen in round 9, i.e. found by Yuna's Whistle on turn 30 itself; only Luminous Broodmoth (seen round 6, held to round 10) was already in hand before that turn.)
